# SIMBA UQ: Similarity-Based Aggregation for Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#simba-uq)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.859.pdf) · Findings of EMNLP 2025 proceedings, pages 15880–15894

**Reading coverage:** All 15 PDF pages, sections 1–5, limitations/ethics, references and appendices A–B; tables 1–5 and rendered figures 2–3/table 1 inspected.

## Research question

Repeated generation agreement is a potential confidence signal, but the relation between agreement and correctness needs a calibrated mapping.

## Method

SIMBA aggregates pairwise similarities through arithmetic averaging, a conditional-independence Bayesian model or supervised random forests. Some variants add log-probability features and therefore are not entirely black-box.

## Evaluation

Nine datasets cover QA, summarization and SQL. SQL uses CodeLlama/Granite outputs on Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD, labeled by execution agreement. Five random half-training/half-test splits evaluate calibration error, top-selection accuracy and AUROC; lower-temperature generations are the main scored outputs.

## What the results support

Learned aggregation improves calibration in the reported in-domain settings; top-selection and AUROC gains can be modest, and Bayesian aggregation sometimes calibrates poorly. Error bars are min/max across five runs, not confidence intervals.

## Limits and qualifications

Results assume stable sampling and suitable in-domain labeled examples; schema-disjoint calibration transfer is not established. Appendix B has ambiguous sample-count wording. Several non-SQL p(true) ACE cells exceed one despite the probability-based definition, so those numerical comparisons require clarification.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful confidence-estimation baselines; calibration is distinct from semantic equivalence, input answerability and a guarantee for individual predictions.
